anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Physical data-model and indexing choices misaligned with workload, forcing inefficient access paths irrespective of statistics or plan selection.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk table or index pages contain logical or physical corruption, making stored structures unreliable and causing inconsistent results.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Host CPU cores are saturated by database processes, leaving inadequate compute capacity for timely query execution.

When these three root causes co-exist, the database exhibits an intertwined symptom set: queries that already rely on sub-optimal or missing indexes are driven to perform full scans; corruption within the scanned pages or index trees forces the optimizer or execution engine to retry, fall back to heap scans, or invoke internal consistency checks, further inflating CPU consumption. Applications observe erratic response times, sudden spikes of CPU utilization, surges in context switches, and intermittent logical errors such as row count mismatches or duplicate key violations. Integrity-check utilities may report corruption while performance tools simultaneously show both index-related inefficiencies and CPU bottlenecks, making single-factor diagnosis misleading.

Causally, poor schema and index design expands I/O and CPU demand because queries traverse more pages and perform additional lookups. The heightened page churn increases the chance of touching corrupted blocks, which in turn triggers error handling, page retries, or forced full-table scans—multiplying CPU work and elongating execution time. The sustained CPU saturation masks the presence of underlying corruption by attributing slowdowns to resource pressure, while corruption-induced scan fallbacks exacerbate the CPU anomaly. Meanwhile, failed or partial index rebuilds caused by corruption can remove valuable indexes, further deepening the design mismatch. The feedback loop among design inefficiency, structural corruption, and CPU exhaustion accelerates performance deterioration and elevates the risk of widespread data inconsistency.

entry.official_description: Schema name '%s' containing upper case characters, used by foreign key '%s' in table '%s.%s', is not allowed with lower_case_table_names = 1.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with logical data inconsistency, structural corruption, uniqueness conflicts, or referential-integrity rules being violated by the workload or storage state.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate data consistency, inspect constraints and index integrity, and check whether data-cleaning, repair, or workload correction is required before retrying.
